name: LocalAI
description: Self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible AI engine (mudler/LocalAI) that runs LLMs, vision, image, and — relevant here — a full voice stack: OpenAI-compatible speech-to-text (/v1/audio/transcriptions), text-to-speech (/tts, /v1/audio/speech), speaker diarization, and WebRTC speech-out. Serves a Go (Fiber) HTTP API plus a web management UI on port 8080. No authentication is enforced by default.
auth_notes: LocalAI enforces no authentication out of the box: with no LOCALAI_API_KEY set, every endpoint and the web UI on :8080 are open. Optional gating exists but is opt-in — LOCALAI_API_KEY=<key> requires an Authorization: Bearer header, and LOCALAI_AUTH=true enables a fuller multi-user mode (admin/user roles, OAuth, per-user keys, usage tracking). Because the quickstart, Docker one-liners, and the bundled web UI all run without a key, the overwhelming majority of self-hosted and demo instances expose the entire API — including model management — unauthenticated.

shodan_dorks.rationale: The LocalAI web UI shell and API landing reference the LocalAI name directly on the canonical port; high-signal name match
Web UI model gallery/management view text; co-occurrence catches instances on non-default ports or behind proxies
Combines the LocalAI name with the OpenAI-compatible audio path advertised in the UI/API surface; isolates instances with the voice/audio stack enabled
Version string surfaced in the web UI footer / API; version-targeted enumeration for CVE scoping

known_vulns: No authentication by default — the entire API and web UI on :8080 are open unless LOCALAI_API_KEY / LOCALAI_AUTH is explicitly set

Unauthenticated model installation — POST /models/apply pulls and installs arbitrary models/backends from the gallery or a supplied URL; a malicious model config can lead to code execution / SSRF on the host
Compute theft — open /v1/chat/completions, /v1/audio/transcriptions, /tts, and /v1/images/generations give free (often GPU-backed) inference and audio synthesis/transcription at operator cost
Audio PII exposure — transcription and diarization endpoints process arbitrary uploaded audio with no auth, consent, or logging in default configs
Voice cloning surface — LocalAI's TTS/voice-clone backends (e.g. VibeVoice) exposed unauthenticated enable arbitrary voice synthesis from operator-hosted voices
Resource-exhaustion DoS — no rate limiting by default; large audio/model operations exhaust GPU VRAM, disk, and bandwidth
Configuration/metrics disclosure — /metrics and model listings enumerate installed backends, model paths, and versions to unauthenticated clients
risk_notes: LocalAI is a broad OpenAI-compatible engine, but its voice stack (STT /v1/audio/transcriptions, TTS /tts + /v1/audio/speech, diarization, WebRTC speech-out) makes an open instance a full unauthenticated voice/audio processing service. Chain: (1) find open :8080 with the LocalAI signature -> (2) enumerate /v1/models and /metrics for installed voice/LLM backends and versions -> (3) abuse the audio + chat + image endpoints for free GPU compute, transcribe attacker audio, synthesize/clone voices, and process (or exfiltrate metadata about) whatever audio the operator routes through it -> (4) escalate via POST /models/apply, installing an attacker-chosen model/backend for potential code execution and SSRF on the host. Because the entire default posture is no-auth and the web UI runs keyless, exposure is common among hobbyist, demo, and 'quick internal tool' deployments. Confirmed added to the corpus as it was not previously present (checked: no prior localai entry).
deployment_notes: Distributed primarily as Docker images (localai/localai, quay.io/go-skynet/local-ai) and single binaries; the API + web UI listen on 8080/tcp (Go Fiber server). CPU-only operation is supported (no GPU required), which broadens where it gets deployed. Models are pulled at runtime from a gallery or arbitrary URLs; the voice stack (whisper-family STT, piper/vibevoice/other TTS, diarization) is enabled per-model. Default runs have no API key; LOCALAI_API_KEY and LOCALAI_AUTH must be opted into. Internet exposure results from users publishing 8080 for a 'private ChatGPT' / internal tool without fronting it with auth or a proxy. Overlaps the OpenAI-compatible inference space (vLLM, Ollama, etc.) but is called out here for its integrated, unauthenticated voice/audio endpoints.
